title: AI Pricing Impact Simulator
tagline: Model price changes before you announce them.
businessOutcomes: Price changes can be tested before you announce them.
summary: Simulates the revenue and profit impact of price increases, churn sensitivity, segment-level pricing, and customer communication strategy.
businessProblem: Owners fear raising prices will lose customers, so they underprice for years — without quantifying how much churn they can absorb and still come out ahead.
outcome: A pricing impact model showing revenue and profit at 0%, 5%, 10%, 15% price increases across assumed churn rates, plus recommended rollout and messaging approach.
expectedOutcomes: A pricing impact model showing revenue and profit at 0%, 5%, 10%, 15% price increases across assumed churn rates, plus recommended rollout and messaging approach.
whoItsFor: Service businesses with stable customer bases considering their first price increase in 1–3 years.
aiInputs: Current average price by service or product tier
Customer count and monthly transaction volume
Proposed price increase percentages to test
aiOutputs: Revenue and profit matrix: price increase % × churn %
Break-even churn rate for each price increase level
Segment recommendations (which services to raise first)
noCodeTools: Pricing impact spreadsheet + ChatGPT sensitivity table
Claude analysis with POS export pasted in
Manual cohort model in Google Sheets with GPT narrative
lowCodeTools: n8n: Square export → Sheets → OpenAI pricing report
Airtable price tiers + GPT communication drafts
Retool pricing simulator with GPT insights
customBuildStack: POS API for current pricing and volume data
Monte Carlo or grid sensitivity model
OpenAI for communication draft and narrative
implementationSteps: Export current price list and volume by service from POS
Estimate current churn rate from customer records
Build sensitivity grid: price increase vs churn assumptions
Identify inelastic services (high demand, low price sensitivity)
Draft customer email using AI with owner review
Plan phased rollout with grandfathering for annual members
systemBehavior: On-demand simulation — does not change live prices
Uses owner-provided churn assumptions with explicit ranges
Generates communication drafts for approval only
Flags services where margin is already healthy vs underpriced
Not competitive pricing intelligence or legal pricing advice
risks: Churn assumptions are guesses until you test — model shows ranges, not certainty
Grandfathered members create complexity the simple model may miss
Regulated industries (healthcare) may have pricing constraints
